title: Token n-gram lexical memory
summary: Attach a trainable token-suffix lookup table at final injection and inspect retrieval, projection, gate, and residual addition without requiring a campaign.

steps.explanation: A causal token suffix maps to a table address; its value is projected to D, gated by the hidden state, and added as a residual at final injection.
observe: engram/injection/final and first lookup addresses in a full probe diagnostic

prerequisites: Prepare the selected tokenizer only for an initialized probe; prepare data before training.
try_changes: Predict the address and [B,T,M] value shapes before probing.
Change one knob: final versus embedding injection, table size, order 2 versus 3, or hash heads.
Treat collision_count as repeated addresses, not proof of semantic collisions.
limits: The table is trainable lexical parameter storage, not executable semantic memory or a frozen pack.
Tokenizer-specific addresses, repeated offline transcripts, and fresh initialization make no transfer or score claim.

papers.title: Engram: A Neural Memory System for Language Models
papers.claim_boundary: Engram motivates lookup-memory questions; SparseLab's trainable token n-gram table is a local educational implementation, not a reproduction.
